title: Central Bureau of Investigation v. Harshad Shantilal Mehta & Ors. (1992 Securities Scam)
crime_type: Financial Fraud / Securities Scam / Criminal Breach of Trust
court_or_authority: Special Court (Securities Transactions) Bombay / Supreme Court of India
source: Supreme Court of India & Indian Kanoon (doc/1922365)
ipc_sections: Section 409 IPC (Criminal breach of trust by public servant/banker)
Section 420 IPC (Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property)
Section 471 IPC (Using as genuine a forged document)
evidence: Forged Bank Receipts (BRs) issued without backing government securities from Bank of Karad and Metropolitan Co-operative Bank
Routing slips tracing thousands of crores from National Housing Bank (NHB) and State Bank of India into broker personal accounts
Extensive audit trails by the Janakiraman Committee documenting artificial price inflation in targeted stock scripts
modus_operandi: Exploited structural loopholes in the inter-bank ready-forward (RF) government securities market. Colluded with bank officials to issue fake Bank Receipts (BRs) unsupported by actual securities. Siphoned bank funds into private brokerage accounts to aggressively ramp up and corner stock equity prices on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
personality_disorder: Grandiose narcissism, manipulative charisma, hyper-optimistic risk blindness, and corporate hubris.
common_traits: Suborning senior banking executives and treasury managers
Aggressive artificial market inflation and pump-and-dump mechanics
summary: The 1992 securities scam involved diversion of over ₹4,000 crore from banking institutions into the stock market. Led to the establishment of SEBI as an empowered regulatory authority and dedicated Special Courts under the 1992 Act.
